entries.what_happened: One manuscript in this family: 'A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound' (OpenAI, dated 25 September 2026). It claims the main theorem of the Introduction: there are absolute constants η, c₁ > 0 and an integer n₀ ≥ 3 such that Δ(n) ≥ c₁·n^(−2+η) for every integer n ≥ n₀, where Δ(n) is the largest, over n-point sets P in the unit square, of the smallest triangle area determined by P. The abstract states the same as: for every sufficiently large n one can place n points in the unit square with every determined triangle of area at least c₁·n^(−2+η). The manuscript gives the exponent explicitly as η = 2/(45435k+16) for an integer k ≥ 2 (Section 8, equation alt:exponent); k = 2 gives η = 1/45443, about 2.2×10⁻⁵. The construction works over prime-indexed sizes n_r ≈ r^α with α = 45435k+16, using a field-norm determinant obstruction over F_{r^41}, integral columns lifted from residues modulo h = B^k and a second prime q, a random sample of 2n_r such columns, and deletion of one index from each violating pair or triple (Sections 3–8). Interpolation to every large n uses a Bertrand-type prime-interval lemma (Appendix). The manuscript also states that this disproves the almost-n^(−2) upper-bound formulation: for every ε > 0 it asks for C_ε with Δ(n) ≤ C_ε·n^(−2+ε), and taking ε = η/2 contradicts the lower bound. The prior lower bound it improves is Komlós–Pintz–Szemerédi's Δ(n) ≫ (log n)/n², which the Introduction recalls. The manuscript does not claim any new upper bound on Δ(n); it cites Komlós–Pintz–Szemerédi (n^(−8/7+ε)) and Cohen–Pohoata–Zakharov (n^(−7/6+ε)) only as background.
entries.delivers: A lower-bound improvement only, for the unit square, which is the container in the list's working reading. Its definition of Δ(n) (maximum over P ⊂ [0,1]² with |P| = n of the minimum over unordered distinct triples of Area(pqr); collinear triples give 0) matches that reading. If correct, it establishes Δ(n) ≥ c₁·n^(−2+η) for all n ≥ n₀ with η = 2/(45435k+16), k ≥ 2 an integer. Only η is explicit; c₁ and n₀ are existence claims, and the constants A_k, D_k, C_k are introduced as 'fixed constants' without computation. This converts the earlier log factor into a power gain n^η, and it refutes the almost-n^(−2) upper-bound formulation, which the list's problem does not itself ask about. The statement of the problem as the list gives it asks for improved lower and upper bounds on the order of Δ(n). The manuscript settles only the lower-bound half, and only as a power gain with a very small exponent. It does not claim to settle the problem.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct: (1) the upper-bound half of the list's question is untouched; the best upper bounds the manuscript cites remain n^(−7/6+ε) (Cohen–Pohoata–Zakharov) and the true order of Δ(n) is not determined; the gap between n^(−2+η) and n^(−7/6+ε) is unchanged in kind. (2) The exponent η ≈ 2×10⁻⁵ is not optimised, and the text says no attempt was made to optimise the construction parameters. (3) The constants c₁ and n₀ are not quantified. (4) Only the unit square is treated; the variant containers the list names as analogues (unit disc, convex regions of unit area, equilateral or right triangles, the cube and higher dimensions, k-gons) are not addressed. (5) Exact small-n values are not addressed.
entries.direction: improves the lower bound by a power (log factor replaced by n^η); disproves the almost-n^(−2) upper-bound formulation
entries.object: Not explicit. The n points are chosen by existence: a random sample of 2n_r integral columns projected to [0,1)² (built from random field labels, digit matrices, auxiliary residues and lifts) has expected number of violating pairs and triples EZ = o(n_r), so some outcome has Z < n_r; deleting one index per violation and keeping any n of the remaining points gives the set. Algebraic structure (the field-norm polynomial and the Chinese remainder theorem over h and q) is explicit, but the final point set is picked from a probability space rather than given by a formula.
entries.doubts: No step is flagged as sketched or conjectural, and the abstract and the main theorem agree. Points in the text that bear on how far the statement is quantified: (i) only the exponent η is explicit, while n₀ and c₁ are asserted to exist through the constants A_k, D_k and C_k, which the text does not compute; (ii) the zero-determinant case is handled by an auxiliary construction which the text says is proved in a later section (Section 7); (iii) the Introduction records that two other preprints (Ellmann 2025, Agama 2026) claim stronger power lower bounds but have flagged unproved steps; the manuscript does not rely on those preprints, and the remark concerns those claims rather than this one.
